newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 10.

text.p: Two of Mexico's crude shipping ports remained closed for a second day due to high winds making a total of five Gulf of Mexico ports shut, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its daily report 1000 local/1600 GMT Friday.
Pajaritos, under the jurisdiction of Coatzacoalcos in Veracruz state, was still closed amid relaxed winds between 25 to 35 km per hour. The port shut Thursday at 0850 local/1450 GMT.
Dos Bocas in Tabasco state closed at 0925 local/1525 GMT Thursday, and was expected to remain closed Friday amid winds of 40 to 50 km per hour, port captain Jorge Rojano Rodriguez said.
The largest of Mexico's crude ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, reopened as wind speeds declined Friday at 0813 local/1413 GMT after a 10-hour closure.

Pajaritos ships an average 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude and Dos Bocas exports 300,000 bpd, according to the latest oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) statistics. Cayo Arcas ships an average 600,000 bpd.
Tabasco port Frontera and Ciudad del Carmen and Campeche state were closed amid winds between 20 and 40 km per hour.
Sailing was closed to smaller boats at Veracruz, Tuxpan, Puerto Madero, Progreso and Cozumel because of high winds.
The report also warned against sailing in the Gulf of Mexico, Gulf of Tehuantepec, Campeche sound and Yucatan peninsula because of winds, rain and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Light rains along the coasts of Jalisco, Colima, Michoacan, Guerrero and Oaxaca states.
